findings.title: Same concurrent-delete NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The fix handles modelSupplier.get() returning null in getSubGroupsCount when a cached group is deleted before its database delegate is loaded, but the three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still dereference modelSupplier.get() unconditionally. The same cache-hit/delegate-miss race therefore still throws NullPointerException and produces a server error when subgroups of a concurrently deleted group are listed or searched. These overloads should return an empty stream, or otherwise handle a null delegate consistently.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null instead of a valid count
findings.body: When the delegate group no longer exists, this returns null, whereas the persistent GroupModel implementations return a numeric count (0 when there are no subgroups). The null is propagated by GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount, so API consumers expecting a number receive no count and any caller that unboxes getSubGroupsCount() will still throw NullPointerException, only later. Returning 0L for a deleted group preserves the method contract and the representation.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, making the concurrency test racy and leaky
findings.body: The reader thread started at line 139 is never joined and there is no latch guaranteeing it has performed a read before deletions begin. The main thread sets deletedAll at line 155 and immediately asserts at line 157 while a read may still be in flight, so a late exception can be missed; conversely the thread may not have run at all before deletion finishes, giving false confidence. The unjoined non-daemon thread can also outlive the test and keep calling managedRealm.admin() during realm cleanup or subsequent tests, causing interference and flakiness. The test should signal that reading has started and join the thread before asserting.
